question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}3 \ln{\left(\frac{u}{v} \right)} \\ 2 u v\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=3 \ln{\left(\frac{u}{v} \right)}$ and $y=2 u v$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=\frac{3}{u}, & x_v&=- \frac{3}{v}, \\ y_u&=2 v, & y_v&=2 u.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{3}{u} & - \frac{3}{v} \\ 2 v & 2 u\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(\frac{3}{u}\right)\left(2 u\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- \frac{3}{v}\right)\left(2 v\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(3,1)&=\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 2 & 6\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(1\right)\left(6\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(-3\right)\left(2\right) \\ &=6-\left(-6\right) \\ &=12.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}- u v \\ - \frac{2 v}{u}\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=- u v$ and $y=- \frac{2 v}{u}$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=- v, & x_v&=- u, \\ y_u&=\frac{2 v}{u^{2}}, & y_v&=- \frac{2}{u}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}- v & - u \\ \frac{2 v}{u^{2}} & - \frac{2}{u}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- v\right)\left(- \frac{2}{u}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- u\right)\left(\frac{2 v}{u^{2}}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(2,-1)&=\begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 \\ - \frac{1}{2} & -1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(1\right)\left(-1\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(-2\right)\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right) \\ &=-1-\left(1\right) \\ &=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}- 2 u v - 2 v^{2} \\ - u + v\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=- 2 u v - 2 v^{2}$ and $y=- u + v$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=- 2 v, & x_v&=- 2 u - 4 v, \\ y_u&=-1, & y_v&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}- 2 v & - 2 u - 4 v \\ -1 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- 2 v\right)\left(1\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- 2 u - 4 v\right)\left(-1\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(0,3)&=\begin{vmatrix}-6 & -12 \\ -1 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(-6\right)\left(1\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(-12\right)\left(-1\right) \\ &=-6-\left(12\right) \\ &=-18.\end{aligned}
$$
